dataset_name: QR Shield reviewed PhishTank suspicious-source QR reproductions
description: A redacted evaluation set linking reviewed public phishing records to safe, redistributable QR reproductions. Original potentially live URLs and incident QR images are not committed.
selection_method: Select every suspicious PhishTank record in the locked Phase 3 validation split whose frozen url.vet observation completed. Selection uses source and completion status only, not score, verdict, or final decision.

source.label_definition: PhishTank marked each selected source URL as verified phishing and online in the locked retrieval snapshot. The project did not open the destinations during review.

safety_rules: Do not commit, print, log, or manually open an original source URL.
Render original source URLs as QR codes only in memory while auditing the locked local source snapshot.
Keep safe reproduction payloads on the reserved .invalid top-level domain and generate their QR bytes only in memory.
Treat frozen url.vet results as time-stamped evidence, not a current reachability claim.
Do not add personal information, payment credentials, or an incident image without explicit redistribution permission.
limitations: The three ready entries are safe QR payload reproductions generated only in memory, not QR images recovered from the original incidents.
The ready set contains all complete PhishTank observations in the existing validation split, so it is small and completion-biased.
PhishTank supplies the suspicious label and is also used by url.vet, so this is integration evidence rather than independent validation of url.vet.
The provider's verified and online fields describe the 2026-08-12 source snapshot and do not claim the destinations remain online.
The supervisor-provided Australian fraud QR remains pending until the original sample and redistribution decision are available.
